You are a professional biblical lexicographer fluent in Spanish. Translate the following English lexicon entry into Spanish.

Lemma: H7121

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "Call, summon, name; cry out in distress; proclaim publicly; read aloud; invite to a gathering"
  Readable gloss: "A foundational verb of vocal action in Biblical Hebrew, qara' covers the full spectrum from naming a child (Gen 2:19) to crying out to God in anguish (Judg 15:18) to reading the Torah scroll aloud before the assembly (Deut 31:11). Arabic preserves a revealing split: da'a covers calling and summoning while qara'a specializes in reading and recitation — the very root that gives us 'Qur'an.' Korean similarly distinguishes 부르다 (call/name) from 읽다 (read) and 부르짖다 (cry out), confirming that these are genuinely distinct senses within a single lexeme."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "call, summon, name"
    Enriched: The core sense of calling, summoning, or naming (575x). Arabic da'a, Korean 부르다, and Swahili kuita all converge here. Gen 2:19 (Adam naming animals), Gen 22:11 (the angel calling Abraham), and Gen 20:8 (Abimelech summoning servants) illustrate the breadth — from bestowing identity to commanding attention. This is the semantic center from which all other senses radiate.
    Existing Spanish translations: Y-llamó, y-llamó
  Sense 2: "cry out in distress"
    Enriched: Crying out in distress or urgent appeal (69x). Korean 부르짖다/외치다 and Spanish clamar/gritar distinguish this from neutral calling. Judg 15:18 (Samson crying out in thirst) and Judg 16:28 (his final prayer) show the desperate vocal quality. Swahili kupiga kelele ('make a commotion') captures the intensity. The cry is typically directed upward — to God — or outward in alarm.
    Existing Spanish translations: Y-clamaba, Y-clamó, Y-gritó, e-invocó, y-clamó, y-gritó
  Sense 3: "proclaim, announce publicly"
    Enriched: Formal public proclamation or announcement (32x). Korean 선포하다 and Swahili kutangaza mark the official, authoritative register. Exod 33:19 and 34:5-6 (God proclaiming his own name and attributes) show the theological weight this sense carries. Lev 23:2 (proclaiming sacred assemblies) illustrates its ritual-administrative function in Israelite life.
    Existing Spanish translations: Proclama, Proclamaron, clamaste, para-proclamar, proclama, proclamaron, proclamaréis, que-proclamaste, y-proclamó
  Sense 4: "be called, be named (Nifal/Pual)"
    Enriched: Passive: to be called or named (Nifal/Pual, 30x). Arabic du'iya, Korean 불리다, and Swahili -itwa consistently render the passive voice. Gen 48:6 ('they shall be called by the name of their brothers') and Deut 28:10 ('all peoples shall see that you are called by the name of the LORD') show naming as identity-conferral from outside the individual.
    Existing Spanish translations: Y-fueron-llamados, Y-será-llamado, es-invocado, es-llamada, es-llamado, fue-invocado, fue-llamado, invocaba, invocado, llamaba, se-invoca, y-sea-llamado, y-será-llamado, y-serán-llamados, y-serás-llamado
  Sense 5: "read, recite aloud"
    Enriched: Reading a written text aloud or reciting from a scroll (24x). Arabic qara'a — the root of 'Qur'an' — preserves this specific meaning. Korean 읽다 and Swahili kusoma ('study/read') distinguish it from oral calling. Exod 24:7 (Moses reading the Book of the Covenant), Deut 17:19, and Josh 8:34 (Joshua reading the Torah) show this as a public liturgical act.
    Existing Spanish translations: Y-leyeron, Y-leyó, clamó, cuando-leyó, cuando-leía, lee, leyera, leyó, proclamó, y-las-leyó, y-leyeron, y-leyó, y-lo-leyó, y-léelo
  Sense 6: "invite, call to a feast"
    Enriched: Inviting or summoning to a feast, sacrifice, or social gathering (9x). Arabic mad'uww ('invited one') and Korean 초대하다 ('invite') isolate this social-hospitality sense. Exod 34:15 (being invited to eat idol sacrifices) and 1Sam 9:13, 22, 24 (Samuel inviting Saul to the sacrificial banquet) show the verb in convivial contexts where the calling is to shared food and fellowship.
    Existing Spanish translations: K, Y-llamarás, invitado, invitados, invité, los-invitados, y-invitó, y-te-llame
